From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: fíla, filá, filâ, -fila, and Fila

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfaɪlə/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Homophone: phyla

Noun

[edit]

fila

  1. plural of filum

Anagrams

[edit]
  • -afil, Fail, alif, fail

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Latin fīla, neuter plural of fīlum.

Noun

[edit]

fila f (plural files)

  1. file
  2. row
  3. (chess) rank
Derived terms
[edit]
  • en fila
  • fila índia
Related terms
[edit]
  • fil
  • desfilar

Further reading

[edit]
  • “fila”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. inflection of filar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From filo (“son”) + -a (“adjectival marker”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfila/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ila
  • Syllabification: fi‧la

Adjective

[edit]

fila (accusative singular filan, plural filaj, accusative plural filajn)

  1. filial (in the case of the son)

French

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fi.la/
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. third-person singular past historic of filer

Anagrams

[edit]
  • alif

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfi.la/
  • Rhymes: -ila
  • Hyphenation: fì‧la

Etymology 1

[edit]

Probably from filo, or from Latin fila, plural of filum. Compare French file, Portuguese fila.

Noun

[edit]

fila f (plural file)

  1. line, rank
  2. (masonry) row, course (a row of bricks or blocks)
  3. queue (British), line (US)
    Synonym: coda
Related terms
[edit]
  • filo

Noun

[edit]

fila f

  1. plural of filo

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. inflection of filare:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Anagrams

[edit]
  • alif

Latin

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈfiː.ɫa]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈfiː.la]

Noun

[edit]

fīla

  1. nominative/accusative/vocative plural of fīlum

References

[edit]
  • "fila", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)

Macanese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Portuguese filha.

Noun

[edit]

fila (masculine filo, plural fila-fila)

  1. daughter

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Not to be confused with filâ (“to clutch; to grab”).

Derived terms

[edit]
  • filo-fila (“children”, literally “son-daughter”)

References

[edit]
  • https://www.macaneselibrary.org/pub/english/uipatua.htm#f

Norwegian Bokmål

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

fila f

  1. definite singular of fil

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. inflection of file:
    1. past tense
    2. past participle

Norwegian Nynorsk

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

fila (present tense filar/filer, past tense fila/filte, past participle fila/filt, passive infinitive filast, present participle filande, imperative fila/fil)

  1. alternative form of file

Noun

[edit]

fila

  1. definite singular of fil

References

[edit]
  • “fila” in The Nynorsk Dictionary.

Old Polish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (10th–15th CE) /fʲiːlʲa/
  • IPA(key): (15th CE) /fʲilʲa/

Noun

[edit]

fila f

  1. alternative form of chwila

Polish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Lesser Poland):
    • (Goral):
      • (Podhale) IPA(key): [ˈfi.la]

Noun

[edit]

fila f

  1. (Podhale, Pieniążkowice) alternative form of chwila

Further reading

[edit]
  • Jan Karłowicz (1900), “chwila”, in Słownik gwar polskich [Dictionary of Polish dialects] (in Polish), volume 1: A do E, Kraków: Akademia Umiejętności, page 210

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfi.lɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfi.lɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfi.la/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈfi.lɐ/

  • Rhymes: -ilɐ
  • Homophone: filha (Madeira)
  • Hyphenation: fi‧la

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from French file.[1]

Noun

[edit]

fila f (plural filas)

  1. queue (line of people)
  2. queue (waiting list)
  3. (computing) queue (FIFO data structure)
Related terms
[edit]
  • fio

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. inflection of filar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

References

[edit]
  1. ^ “fila”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Further reading

[edit]
  • “fila”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from German Fülle.

Noun

[edit]

fȉla f (Cyrillic spelling фи̏ла)

  1. (regional) stuffing
    Synonym: nadjev

Related terms

[edit]
  • filati

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfila/ [ˈfi.la]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ila
  • Syllabification: fi‧la

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from French file.

Noun

[edit]

fila f (plural filas)

  1. line, row, rank, file
  2. queue (British), line (US)
    Synonym: cola
  3. (chess) rank
    Antonym: columna
Derived terms
[edit]
  • cerrar filas
  • en fila
  • fila india
  • romper filas
Related terms
[edit]
  • filo
  • hilo

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. inflection of filar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Further reading

[edit]
  • “fila”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
  • “fila”, in Diccionario de americanismos [Dictionary of Americanisms] (in Spanish), Association of Academies of the Spanish Language [Spanish: Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española], 2010

Swahili

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.
Particularly: “TUKI and bab.la suggest English (but what word? foul? vice? vile?) but could it be from Arabic, e.g. سَافِل (sāfil)?”

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio (Kenya):(file)

Noun

[edit]

fila class IX (plural fila class X)

  1. evil, vice

Swedish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

fil +‎ -a

Verb

[edit]

fila (present filar, preterite filade, supine filat, imperative fila)

  1. to file (smooth, grind, or cut with a file)
  2. (figuratively, with på) to work on or polish (something)
    fila på ett manifest
    work on a manifesto

Conjugation

[edit]
Conjugation of fila (weak)
active passive
infinitive fila filas
supine filat filats
imperative fila —
imper. plural1 filen —
present past present past
indicative filar filade filas filades
ind. plural1 fila filade filas filades
subjunctive2 file filade files filades
present participle filande
past participle filad

1 Archaic. 2 Dated. See the appendix on Swedish verbs.

Related terms

[edit]
  • nedfila

References

[edit]
  • “fila”, in Svensk ordbok [Dictionary of Swedish] (in Swedish)
  • “fila”, in Svenska Akademiens ordlista [Wordlist of the Swedish Academy] (in Swedish)
  • “fila”, in Svenska Akademiens ordbok [Dictionary of the Swedish Academy] (in Swedish)

Tetum

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

fila

  1. to turn

Yoruba

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Ultimately from Hausa fū̀lā, perhaps through Nupe fùla.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fì.là/

Noun

[edit]

fìlà

  1. hat, cap (in particular) the traditional Yoruba caps worn by males.
    Synonyms: ètú, àkòó
